safety:
To help stay safe while working in hot conditions, follow these precautions:
- Drink water regularly while working in the heat. [NIOSH_001_CHUNK_006]
- Take rest breaks during hot working conditions. [NIOSH_001_CHUNK_006]
- Increase time working in the heat gradually when getting acclimatized. [NIOSH_001_CHUNK_004]
- Recognize symptoms of heat-related illness and follow workplace emergency procedures. [NIOSH_001_CHUNK_003]

Official evidence:
[NIOSH_001_CHUNK_006] https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/recommendations/index.html
[NIOSH_001_CHUNK_004] https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/recommendations/index.html
[NIOSH_001_CHUNK_003] https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/heat-stress/recommendations/index.html

These are general precautions, not a substitute for a workplace heat-risk assessment.

index:
Heat index combines air temperature and relative humidity to describe how hot the weather feels.

Higher humidity can make hot weather feel hotter because sweat evaporates less effectively.

Official evidence:
[NOAA_001_CHUNK_001] https://www.weather.gov/safety/heat-index
